title: Benatar's Anti-Natalism & The Ethics of Procreation
rootClaim: Bringing new sentient human beings into existence is always a net harm and morally wrong.

branches.text: The Asymmetry of Pleasure and Pain dictates that non-existence is strictly preferable to existence.

children.text: Benatar's Asymmetry: Pain is bad and pleasure is good; but the absence of pain is good even if no one exists to enjoy it, whereas the absence of pleasure is not bad unless someone is deprived.
Symmetrical Evaluation Counter: If no one exists to suffer the absence of pleasure, then equally no one exists to benefit from the absence of pain.
Duty Asymmetry: We feel a duty not to bring suffering children into existence, but no duty to create happy children to experience pleasure.
Consent Violation: Procreation imposes guaranteed existential risks, suffering, and inevitable mortality on a person who never gave prior consent.
Hypothetical Consent: Most existing people are glad to be alive, implying retroactive consent for the choice to bring them into existence.
Optimism Bias (Pollyanna Principle): Human psychological adaptation systematically underestimates personal suffering and overestimates life quality.

branches.text: Procreation is a positive good that creates net flourishing, moral agency, and meaningful life experiences.

children.text: Overall Positive Goods: Deep human relationships, creative accomplishments, joy, and discovery outweigh the ordinary burdens of suffering for most individuals.
Chronic Vulnerability: Extreme pain, disease, bereavement, and aging are guaranteed structural components of all biological lives.
Extinction Consequences: Universal adoption of anti-natalism leads to voluntary human extinction, eliminating all future culture, moral progress, and consciousness.
Harm-Free Extinction: A painless phase-out of the species causes zero suffering to unborn generations, fulfilling the ultimate utilitarian harm reduction.

definitions.description: The philosophical claim that there is an asymmetry between pain and pleasure such that coming into existence is always a serious harm.
The psychological tendency for people to remember pleasant items more accurately than unpleasant ones and rate their own lives as happier than objective metrics suggest.
The ethical position that assigns a negative value to birth and argues procreation is morally wrong.
The principle that prospective parents should choose to create children who are expected to have the best possible life.
